newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Malaysia to ask Bangladesh to cut palm oil tariff.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to ask Bangladesh to cut palm oil tariff.

text.p: Malayasian Palm Oil Promotion Council (MPOPC) will urge Bangladesh to cut import tariffs on palm oil, MPOPC chief executive Mohammad Yusof Hashim said on Sunday.
"We will request the government (Bangladesh) to reduce the tariff further to 30 percent," he told a news conference.
He said Bangladesh had already cut the import duty on palm oil to 35 percent from 45 percent recently, "realising its growing demand in the domestic market."
Bangladesh imported 102,887 tonnes of palm oil in 1996 calendar year against only 15,227 tonnes in the previous year.
A.K.M. Fakhrul Alam, the MPOPC representative in Bangladesh, said Bangladesh's palm oil imports might rise to 120,000 tonnes in 1997.
The market share of the imported palm oil is 30 percent against 70 percent by Soyabean oil in 1996, he said.
Per capita consumption of edible oil in Bangladesh is 4.5 kilograms compared with a 15 kg globaly.
